title: Mount a boring bar in a lathe tool holder and clamp it with its two set screws
instruction: Mount the boring bar in its holder, ready to bore this hole to full depth.
context: Machinists mount and set a boring bar at every lathe setup that bores a hole, and it is among the first things an apprentice learns. The bar goes into the holder's bore from the chuck side and is clamped by set screws on its flat. The overhang is the decision: the bar must reach the bottom of the hole with the holder still clear of the workpiece, but a steel bar should stick out no more than about four times its diameter, because chatter and deflection grow steeply with overhang and a long bar leaves a rough, oversize bore. The cutting edge must also face the right way and the flat must face the screws, or the bar can turn in the clamp.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top (arm bases at y +305 and y -305). A bench lathe stand-in, real size, axis horizontal along y at x 250 and 45 above the table. The chuck is toward +y; the operator's side is toward the robot (-x), and this lathe cuts with the edge on that side. Fixed: (1) Tool holder: a steel block 50 (x) by 60 (y, from -20 to 40) by 70 tall. Its face toward the chuck, at y 40, is the face stick-out is measured from. A 12.4 mm bore runs through it on the axis (the chuck-side mouth chamfered in two 1.5 mm steps). Two M6 x 1.0 set screws stand over the bore at y -5 and y 25, each reached through a square hex-key socket in the top face, 5.2 mm across, with a 10 mm mouth, 15 mm deep. Each screw's tip starts 0.2 mm over the top of a round bar seated in the bore. (2) Workpiece: a 50 mm steel round in a chuck (80 mm across, y 310 to 355), its face at y 240, with a blind bore on the axis 22 mm across and 40 mm deep. (3) Rack: two steel blades, y 70 to 150, x 3 to 9 either side of the axis, 39.8 tall. (4) Key stand: a wooden block 30 by 30 by 28 mm at x 190, y -120, with a 3.8 mm hole 24 mm deep. Loose: (5) Boring bar: a 12 mm round steel shank, 150 mm long, 130 g, with a flat 0.8 mm deep along the whole top of the shank and a gold cutting insert, 5 x 3 x 4 mm, in one end, flush with that end's face and 1 mm proud of the shank's side, 90 degrees round from the flat. It lies on the rack on the lathe axis, flat up, its cutting end toward +y at y 205, its plain end at y 55 (15 mm in front of the holder), the insert toward the operator's side. (6) Hex key: a steel 3 mm T-handle key, 60 g, a 60 mm shaft under an 8 mm round crossbar 90 mm long along x, standing in the stand's hole with its tip on the floor of the hole. Set screws: the bore, bar and sockets are real; the screws are a rule (see fidelity). Pitch 1.0 mm.
scoring: Read at the last step from the poses of the bar and key and the grippers (real trial: steel rule, caliper, top and side video). Stick-out s: how far the centre of the bar's cutting-end face is past the holder's chuck-side face along the axis, in mm. The key is in a screw's socket when its tip is within 1.5 mm of the socket's axis, its shaft within 6 degrees of vertical and the tip at least 7 mm under the top face. A screw then turns with the key, clockwise in, one pitch (1.0 mm) a turn. It is TIGHT when it has been turned to meet the bar (0.2 mm down for a bar on its round, 1.0 mm for a bar with its flat up within 10 degrees) and then 0.4 turn more; it needs the bar under it. While any screw is tight the bar's pose is held; with none tight it is free. 1.0: both screws tight; the cutting end toward the chuck (axis within 30 degrees of +y); the flat up within 10 degrees; the insert within 15 degrees of the operator's side; 45 <= s <= 48 mm (reaches the 40 mm depth with 5 mm to spare; at most four times the 12 mm diameter); the key in neither socket; every part of both grippers' fingers at least 3 cm from the bar; and the bar's two ends moved 1 mm or less over the last 1 s. 0.5: both screws tight and the cutting end toward the chuck, but not 1.0 (s outside 45 to 48, flat or insert off, key still in, a gripper near, or moving). 0.25: the bar through the bore (axis within 1.5 mm of the bore's at both faces of the holder, plain end behind the holder, cutting end past its face), cutting end toward the chuck, the screws not both tight. 0 otherwise, and 0 for the rest of the trial if the bar was clamped with its cutting end away from the chuck, or if the bar or key is 5 cm or more below the table top. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Back both screws out, pull the bar and the key. Lay the bar on the rack on the axis, flat up, cutting end toward the chuck with its plain end at y 55 and the insert toward the operator's side; stand the key in its hole. Check the bar slides freely through the bore.
fidelity: Set screws are software: the key's tip in a socket, pushed down and upright, turns a screw (1.0 mm a turn); tight 0.4 turn past contact with the bar; then the bar's pose is held (rewritten every step). Real set screws take several N m; the model needs none. Rigid bodies. The round bore and shank are 20 and 9 flat boxes; the flat is real. Holder, workpiece and rack are fixed: no spindle or slides. Sizes are nominal, not measured on a machine.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0; left arm alone: 0.25; right arm alone: 0.0
